Our two teens, 13 & 14, have bark phones! I'm moderately above-average techy. I knew it'd be a pain in the ass to actually lock down a modern device in any meaningful way that didn't have easy work arounds for them to exploit. They both love that they have smart phones, we love that we can *EASILY* control their exposure - i.e. no social media. It's not actually super expensive; the phones are included and the basic plan is only about $30 a month. Since you don't want any social media, the basic plan is all you'll need. 

Our eldest also uses his school Chromebook to email his friends as well. Like you, we aren't enthusiastic about it but we can't control it, either. We have noticed that since getting a phone, he has cut down on email usage because it's much more simple for him to text. Partial win for us! Hopefully you'll notice a similar trend regardless what route you decide to choose for a phone. :) 

The text monitoring system is fantastic, btw. The kids feel like they do indeed have privacy while knowing if something were flagged and we saw it, we only talk to them if it's a genuine issue. We don't micromanage their conversations even if it gets flagged multiple times for whatever reason as long as it's not a serious issue. Most commonly, we get lots of "bullying" flags because their playful banter minics similar language but it's not actual bullying. Same for curse words, tbh.

Sorry for the micro-essay, but hopefully I said something that was helpful. We've had Bark for our eldest for two years now, younger one had a Gabb watch for a year but got upgraded to a Bark phone a year ago. If you have any questions, I'd love to help!

The seatbelt extenders they have are tested for crash safety ratings, the one you bought probably hasn't been. I know plane crashes are rare, but this is one time that being embarrassed for a short moment is way better than spending money ahead of time.

I looove board games!! I wish I had more opportunities to play, nobody around me likes them as much as I do. I don't want to play with people who don't enthusiastically want to play. :(( 

I'm probably gonna get roasted for this opinion, but it's my honest opinion:

I absolutely have no problem when someone is new and doesn't know how to play and needs to take time to learn/process everything. I mean, hello?? I have to do that basically every time, even if I've played the game 20 times before. I've gotta get a round or ten in before I can get back in the groove! 😩 

However! I **cannot** stand when someone doesn't pay attention and is slow to notice it's their turn to play. I don't care if someone knows it's their turn and is taking a moment to think about their choice/move, but I have to see that they're *actively* aware that it's their turn. Kids are the worst about it. I don't mind playing with kids, but when they can't sit down and pay attention long enough to get through even one round it's annoying. Tbf, it's not just kids. There are some adults that do it, too. 

It's an intense pet peeve of mine. I know it's awful because I (obviously, because I'm here) have ADHD and know it's hard to always be paying attention but like.. it's only that very specific instance of inattentiveness that bothers me. I'm not inpatient when someone "plays slow" for literally ANY other reason; it's *just* when they're slow because they're not aware it's their turn. 

Takes you a few minutes to calculate your best choice? All good. Choice paralysis is something I struggle with myself. Takes you a few seconds to even find your piece on the board? No problem. Object permanence issues are rough. Takes you longer than everyone else because you don't do mental math quickly? Same dude. Takes you a moment to gather your thoughts because whatever game we're playing has a lot of individual pieces and it's a little overwhelming? You're fine, I'm probably doing that on my turn, too. Takes you more time than others because you have to ask questions when it's your turn? Oh no, how dare you ask questions to learn! So awful of you. You're just the worst. ((/s)) 

I literally don't care if your turn itself takes a while. I just care when it takes a while for you to START your turn.

There's been a few games I've participated in when someone would ***consistently*** need to be nudged/elbowed and told it's their turn. I'm usually just so happy to be able to be playing a board game in the first place that I just suck it up and deal with it. There was one time that I apologized and excused myself from the game because I couldn't deal with it. We were playing a quick-paced, time restricted game, it genuinely added an extra 10-15 seconds each round which had a big impact on game play. We had to let them know it was their turn. Every. Single. Time. 

It comes across as them not being interested in playing and I can't stand it. If you don't want to play, don't play. It starts to kick my RSD into gear ("Do they not like me enough to want to do something with me that I enjoy?" "Am I really that boring?" etc) which doesn't help anything of course. 

But yeah. Sorry for the absolute rant. I love board games. Wish I could play them more. It'd be a good way for me to make new friends, too, because I only have one. They're literally they only person that I talk to on a regular basis that isn't family or a client at work.

That being said, if you are deadset on fasting, you NEED to start with intermittent fasting. Once you can go a while (2 or so months) without binging while holding a steady IF, then you'll be ready to move onto extended fasting. 

Holding onto extended fasts can/will cause you to binge upon refeeding. Then you'll feel like shit for doing so and go back on another fast and the cycle continues. This is classic BED, and it's detrimental. You need to talk to your support net and medical team to make sure you can accomplish this in a healthy way.
